svg.title: Contract-first HTTP filters
svg.desc: At build time, the specification-repository-http jar ships the OpenAPI fragment META-INF/specrepo/openapi/specrepo-filters.yaml with the parameters SpecrepoFilter, SpecrepoOrFilter and SpecrepoSort, the schemas SpecrepoFilterOperator and SpecrepoInvalidFilterProblem, and the response SpecrepoInvalidFilter. A Gradle Copy task, extractSpecrepoFragment, copies it next to the service's own OpenAPI contract so that each $ref resolves. The contract references those components from its searchProducts operation, declares its 400 response as SpecrepoInvalidFilter and documents the allowed fields with x-specrepo-filterable-fields or a pattern. OpenAPI Generator turns the contract into the interface ProductsApi, whose searchProducts method receives filter, orFilter and sort as List<String>, each null when the client did not send it. At run time, ProductsController implements ProductsApi and calls search.toPlan, which copies the non-null lists into a parameter map and calls the auto-configured HttpFilterParser: parser.toQueryPlan(Product.class, params, POLICY, Set.of("name")), then POLICY.validate(plan), so a disallowed field fails before the query. The parser applies the limits and operators configured with specrepository.http properties. The allow-list lives in two places: in the contract it is documentation that a client can ignore, and the AllowedFieldsPolicy in Java is what the server enforces, so both are reviewed together. The plan then goes to repository.query(plan), which adds the server condition tenantId equal to the current tenant, kept out of the allow-list, and runs findAll. A filter error from the parser, from the policy or from the query is answered by HttpFilterProblemDetailsExceptionHandler with 400 Bad Request and an application/problem+json body, the SpecrepoInvalidFilter response that the contract declares. The animation shows the fragment flowing into the contract and the generated interface, a request filtering on status reaching the repository, and a request filtering on tenantId rejected with a 400 whose detail is: Field 'tenantId' is not allowed for filtering.
